title: PM shift — runtime daylog (Zoe)
content:
PM shift notes — quick brain dump

Context: covering afternoon shift for runtime triage. Mostly focused on KV cache behaviour and a small kernel regression flagged by perf tests. Quick notes so I don't forget details for the 15:00 deep dive with Mina.

Observations (so far):
- 99p token latency spiked ~18% between 09:40-10:05 UTC on gpu-pool-3. Spike correlated with a drop in KV cache hit rate.
- KV cache hit rate fell from ~82% -> ~63% for model redwood-mini-13b-quant under the conv-h 512 profile.
- Error rate (503) for runtime-proxy was ~0.2% during the spike; most 503s timestamped to proxy->runtime timeouts.

Immediate repro steps (what I ran):
1) Ran the short loadtest locally: ./bin/loadtest --model redwood-mini-13b-quant --profile conv-h-512 --rps 150 --duration 5m
2) While loadtest ran, dumped kv cache keys (see command below) and sampled latencies with the tracing hook.

Quick commands I used:
- kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-proxy-7f5 -c runtime --since=45m | grep -i timeout
- python tools/kvcache_dump.py --pool gpu-pool-3 --top=200 > /tmp/kv_dump_20260311.txt
- ./bin/tracer sample --span runtime.infer --duration 2m > /tmp/trace_20260311.json

Findings from dumps:
- Top evicted keys show a pattern: a handful of prompt prefixes account for most evictions (multi-tenant churn).
- Some eviction timestamps line up with large batched requests from a single internal client; need to confirm which customer.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Is the eviction implemented purely LRU or is it size-weighted? (quick scan of code suggests LRU with size heuristics, but not 100% sure)
- Was PR #842 (shader/kernel memory change) landed before the first spike? Timeline: PR merged 2026-03-09.
- Are we seeing cascading timeouts because of proxy thread saturation or because of runtime kernel stalls?

TODO (priority order):
- [ ] Attach /tmp/kv_dump_20260311.txt to JIRA RINF-1253 (est 20m).
- [ ] Add a short Grafana panel for 'cache_eviction_rate' (owner Rajiv) — useful to detect before latency moves.
- [ ] Run a controlled load test with eviction logging enabled (Mina + me) at 14:00 UTC.
- [ ] Prepare rollback steps for PR 842 (write short runbook, include exact kubectl commands).
- [ ] Confirm which customer/client produced the heavy batched requests (ask SRE to correlate source IP).

Notes to self / runbook snippets:
- To rollback PR 842: kubectl -n runtime set image deploy/runtime-worker runtime=ghcr.io/redwood-inference/runtime:pre-842 && kubectl rollout status deploy/runtime-worker -w
- To avoid noisy restarts: do NOT restart runtime-proxy while loadtest is running; restart worker nodes one at a time, wait for stable traces.

Meeting follow-ups (15:00 deep dive):
- Bring kv dump, sample traces, and the short loadtest config used.
- Ask Mina to bring histogram of kernel exec times (focus on >50ms tail).
- Ask SRE: can they enable packet capture for 2 minutes around next spike window so we can check network blips.

Quick ideas / speculative fixes (brainstorm):
- Micro-binning of KV cache by prompt-hash to reduce cross-tenant eviction (might reduce worst-case churn).
- Add a lightweight bloom filter precheck before inserting into KV cache to reduce writes for low-benefit keys.
- Bump proxy request timeout by 50ms temporarily during canary to avoid premature 503s (careful: hides real backpressure).

Handoff notes for night oncall (Zach):
- If you see a repeat of this pattern, run loadtest-replay with --rps 100 to validate.
- If eviction rate stays high, temporarily scale up gpu-pool-3 by +1 node (ask infra) and monitor 99p.

Random scratch (for future):
- Could we surface 'eviction churn per-tenant' metric in console? Would be useful for customers testing long contexts.

End of shift checklist:
- [ ] Upload kv dump to JIRA
- [ ] Leave short note in #runtime-oncall channel with link to this doc and attachments

-- Zoe
